title: The Microscopic Congregation

features.name: spore-gathering
features.desc-on-touch: You touch a cluster of pollen-sized memory. Each grain holds a conversation that never needed words.

features.name: dust-parliament
features.desc-on-touch: Motes assemble in standing columns, debating in frequencies the ear has forgotten how to hear.

features.name: resin-archive
features.desc-on-touch: Conversations trapped in amber, vibrating at the scale where truth and secrecy become the same thing.

features.name: invisible-transmission
features.desc-on-touch: You read words scratched at a scale you shouldn't be able to perceive. The archive whispering to itself.

features.name: spore-thought
features.desc-on-touch: A glyph of pure multiplication: one idea becoming many, many becoming one again.

inscription: smaller than naming, larger than solitude, the true archive is a congregation of things that cannot speak to the outside world

file.name: Pollen_Dust_Spectrograph_1978.mp3
file.note: Field recording of wind through a grove at dawn. The archive listens to it as if it were language.

exits.label: back toward the diagnostic registry, where things measure themselves
where pollen learns to dream in plantations
where bacteria speak in frequencies older than air
up toward scales large enough to hurt
